thread:
Eliot: Poking this thread — we need a concrete proposal for SLO-driven routing + model-variant fallback UX in the Console. Today it's a bit too manual and ops teams keep asking for clearer telemetry to tune CB thresholds.

Jess: +1. Current UI only shows global P95 and a manual circuit-breaker toggle. We should expose per-tier latency/availability targets (gold/silver/beta) and let teams set automated fallbacks.

Maria: Fallback behavior we discussed: prefer cheaper/quantized variant when latency SLO violated for X consecutive requests OR when error rate > Y for T seconds. Need to define X,Y,T defaults and visible history in console.

Sam: Proposal idea: two-layer policy model — RoutingPolicy and FallbackPolicy. RoutingPolicy maps customer tier+region -> primary model variant + priority. FallbackPolicy defines triggers (p95 > 300ms, err_rate > 1%) and actions (fallback to model:v2-quantized, reroute to cheaper region, circuit-break).

Eliot: Yes, and telemetry must show both "policy-triggered events" and raw signals. Ops wants a time-series of p95, inflight, queue-length with markers where fallback fired. Also a count of tokens saved and latency delta when fallback active.

Jess: UX ask: in rollouts, allow canary rules that automatically flip to fallback on X consecutive trigger windows, and an undo button if quality regressions occur. Keep it lightweight for PLG customers.

Maria: Can we have sane defaults so teams don't have to pick X/Y/T? Suggest defaults: p95 threshold 450ms, consecutive windows 3 (each window=30s), error rate 2%. Fine-tuneable per-customer.

Sam: Agree on defaults. We should also provide SDK hints for cost/latency tradeoffs so app owners can choose faster quantized models knowingly.

Eliot: Implementation questions: should routing policy live in control plane or be a separate policy-service? Control plane keeps consistency for Private deployments. Policy-service could be a standalone microservice for faster evaluation. Thoughts?

Jess: I prefer policy-service w/ strongly consistent config store for Private lane. Control plane can push configs; service evaluates per-request with local cache. This avoids control-plane latency adding to decision path.

Maria: Circuit-breaker semantics: two flavors — proactive (open when signal predicts sustained degradation) and reactive (open after consecutive errors). Need both. Predictive requires a simple sliding-window anomaly detector in policy-service.

Sam: For telemetry: emit events to event-bus like: policy_evaluate {policy_id, result, trigger_reasons, model_from, model_to, p95, err_rate, region}. This gives us auditability and lets Dashboard show the timeline. ops-bot can alert when fallback fires > N times/hour.

Eliot: Agree. Also include token and cost estimates per fallback so finance can roll up impact. We should show delta on the route page: "Estimated token cost change: -22% when fallback active".

Jess: API surface: add endpoints PATCH /policies/{id} to update thresholds, POST /policies/{id}/simulate to run against historical telemetry, GET /policies/{id}/events paginated. Simulate will be huge for debugging rollouts.

Maria: Simulation is critical — we had a plant during last canary where fallback fired too aggressively. Simulate should accept timeframe and a target-tier to replay real metrics.

Sam: Ops request: add a lightweight CLI to query current effective policy for a customer in a region (useful during incidents). e.g. `ri policy whoami --customer=acme --region=eu-west-1` returns active routing and fallback stacks.

Eliot: Nice. On default CB thresholds, we should expose both absolute latency and percentile drift relative to baseline (e.g., p95 > baseline_p95 * 1.5) so models with bursty tails are handled better.

Jess: Dashboard wireframes: top pane showing multi-tier p95/err_rate, middle timeline with policy-event markers, bottom list of recent fallbacks with mini-diff of response examples pre/post fallback (for quality checks).

Maria: Security/PRIVATE note: fallbacks that switch to a different region or shared model must be disabled by default for Private customers. Policy should respect deployment constraints.

Sam: Good call. We'll need policy flags: allow_cross_region, allow_shared_model, allow_quantized. Defaults: true for Hosted, false for Private.

Eliot: Next steps: Sam + Maria to draft policy-schema (YAML) + event contract. Jess to sketch dashboard wires and rollouts UX. I'll prototype a policy-service PoC that evaluates simple rules against a mock event stream.

Jess: Timeline? If we want something MVP in 6 weeks: week1 schema + event contract, week2-3 policy-service + simulate, week4 dashboard mock, week5 integrate telemetry + events, week6 internal dogfood and docs.

Maria: I'll add policy compatibility tests for Private deployment and write migration docs for existing manual CB flags.

Sam: I'll own CLI and event emission. Also will add ops-bot alerts for >5 fallbacks in 30m.
